descripcion_geo: Deep canyon and river that flows into the Dead Sea in the east; border between Moab and Amorites.
importancia_estrategica: Transjordan natural border; boundary between the Moabite and Amorite territory that Israel had to cross.

historias.descripcion: Israel crosses the Arnon River on its way through the Transjordan towards Canaan, entering Amorite territory.

historias.titulo: The Arnon as a promised border
historias.descripcion: God sets the Arnon as the southern border of the territory that Israel will conquer east of the Jordan.

historias.titulo: The Book of the Lord's Wars
historias.descripcion: An ancient poem cited in the Book of the Lord's Wars mentions the Arnon as the scene of the battles of Israel.

personajes.descripcion: He led Israel across the Arnon on the march to Canaan.
He rejected the passage of Israel and was defeated; Their territory (north of the Arnon) was given to Reuben and Gad.
The Mesa Stele mentions the Arnon as the northern border of Moab.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: The Arnon was the first natural obstacle that Israel overcame in Transjordan; Their crossing inaugurated the sequence of victories that prepared the conquest of Canaan.

judaismo.descripcion: The crossing of the Arnon begins the conquest of the Transjordan; prefigures the crossing of the Jordan.
judaismo.significado_teologico: The crossing of the Arnon begins the conquest of the Transjordan; prefigures the crossing of the Jordan.
